title: Legal practice

basis.cite: Fed. R. Civ. P. 5.2(a); Fed. R. Crim. P. 49.1
basis.summary: Court filings may include only the last four digits of an SSN, taxpayer ID or financial account number, the year of birth, and a minor's initials. The criminal rule adds: city and state only of a home address.

basis.cite: ABA Model Rule of Professional Conduct 1.6
basis.summary: A lawyer shall not reveal information relating to the representation of a client. This is far broader than identifiers.

identifiers.treatment: remove; city and state may stay
remove: a docket number identifies the parties in a public search

caveats: Privilege and Rule 1.6 attach to the facts of the matter. A memo with every name removed can still be confidential and identifiable from its facts.
Rule 5.2 is a filing rule; it says what a public filing may contain, not what may be shared with a third-party service.
note: A starting point drawn from the cited texts, not legal advice. Have counsel confirm the list for your jurisdiction and use before relying on it.
